tools.name: mailboxes_list
tools.description: List the connected mailboxes that answer, each by the name a tool's mailbox input takes, and the tools its provider does not offer. The mail of every mailbox mailboxes_list names is read and written with Multi Mail's tools.

tools.name: messages_list
tools.description: Search one connected mailbox in its own provider's query language, Gmail's or Outlook's. The mail of every mailbox mailboxes_list names is read and written with Multi Mail's tools.

tools.name: messages_list_all_mailboxes
tools.description: Search every mailbox you have connected in one call. The answer names the mailbox each result came from, names any mailbox it could not search, and is merged newest first by when each message arrived, a thread by its newest. The mail of every mailbox mailboxes_list names is read and written with Mul

tools.name: threads_get
tools.description: Read every message of one thread in a connected mailbox, oldest first.

tools.name: messages_get
tools.description: Read one message in a connected mailbox, with its headers and its body.

tools.name: drafts_create
tools.description: Compose a message in a connected mailbox and keep it there as a draft.

tools.name: drafts_update
tools.description: Change a draft in a connected mailbox. A field the call leaves out stays as the draft has it. A mailbox whose provider is imap keeps the edited draft under a new id the answer names, and the old id then reads nothing; an old version its server did not remove stays in Drafts, named as previousVersion

tools.name: drafts_reply
tools.description: Compose a reply to a message as a draft, inside the thread it answers and quoting it below the reply: to whoever wrote it, or with replyAll to everyone on it. Nothing leaves the mailbox until the draft is sent.

tools.name: drafts_forward
tools.description: Compose a forward of a message as a draft, with the files it carries and inside the thread it already sits in. Nothing leaves the mailbox until the draft is sent.

tools.name: drafts_delete
tools.description: Throw away a draft. Nothing already sent is touched. Gmail mailboxes only: an Outlook draft keeps its identifier once sent, so discarding one could delete sent mail.

tools.name: messages_send
tools.description: Compose a new message in a connected mailbox and send it in one call. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id already spent sends nothing again: the answer says whether that send went or may have gone.

tools.name: drafts_send
tools.description: Send a draft. It leaves the mailbox and consumes the draft. Only a draft is sent: a message already sent or received is refused, and nothing leaves. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id already spent sends nothing

tools.name: messages_reply
tools.description: Reply to a message, inside its own thread and quoting it below the reply: to whoever wrote it, or with replyAll to everyone on it. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id already spent sends nothing again: the answer

tools.name: messages_forward
tools.description: Forward one message to the addresses you name, with the files it carries, inside the thread it already sits in. Only the provider's own limit applies to what it carries. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id alread

tools.name: labels_list
tools.description: List the labels a connected mailbox holds, by the id each is applied by. A mailbox whose provider is imap holds its folders as labels, nested by /, beside UNREAD, STARRED and SPAM.

tools.name: labels_create
tools.description: Create a label in a connected mailbox and answer the id it is applied by. In a Gmail mailbox, and as a folder in one whose provider is imap, a / nests it under the label before it, made first where missing; in an Outlook mailbox a / is just a character.

tools.name: labels_update
tools.description: Rename a label, recolour it, or both. The id comes from labels_list. An Outlook mailbox's categories are its labels, and Microsoft lets one take only a new colour. A mailbox whose provider is imap renames its folder, which takes no colour, and answers the label's new id.

tools.name: labels_delete
tools.description: Delete one label, by its id from labels_list. No message is deleted: in a Gmail mailbox the label comes off every message; an Outlook mailbox's category leaves its list, and the messages that carried it keep its name. A mailbox whose provider is imap deletes only a folder holding no mail and no fold

tools.name: threads_modify
tools.description: Apply and remove labels on one thread, or one message of it - an Outlook mailbox's categories are its labels. The ids come from labels_list. Adding SPAM junks it, and taking SPAM off brings it back to the inbox. In a Gmail mailbox adding TRASH bins it too; an Outlook mailbox takes UNREAD and STARRED

tools.name: threads_archive
tools.description: Take one thread out of the inbox. It stays in the mailbox and in search. A mailbox whose provider is imap moves its inbox messages into its archive folder, made as Archive where it has none, each under a new id the answer names.

tools.name: threads_trash
tools.description: Move one thread, or one message of it, to the trash - Gmail's bin, an Outlook mailbox's Deleted Items, the trash folder of a mailbox whose provider is imap - where it stays until threads_untrash brings it back or the provider's own retention ends it. In a mailbox whose provider is imap each moved me

tools.name: threads_untrash
tools.description: Bring one thread, or one message of it, back out of the trash. A mailbox whose provider is imap puts a draft back in its drafts, the owner's own mail in sent mail and the rest in the inbox, each under a new id the answer names.

tools.name: messages_attachments_get
tools.description: Read one attachment of a message. The answer is what it says, as plain text; with as original it is the file itself, base64. messages_get and threads_get name a message's attachments and their sizes. Either answer names the address the original is served at whole, to a GET carrying this same credent

tools.name: settings_filters_list
tools.description: List the rules a connected mailbox files incoming mail by.

tools.name: settings_filters_create
tools.description: Create a rule that files incoming mail in a connected mailbox. A rule that carries mail out of the mailbox, or that bins or junks what it matches, is refused, whether or not the provider would take it. An Outlook mailbox's rule files only under labels or out of the inbox (removeLabelIds INBOX).

tools.name: settings_filters_delete
tools.description: Delete one rule by its id. Mail it already filed stays where it is.

tools.name: settings_send_as_patch
tools.description: Replace the signature on the mailbox's own send-as identity. Nothing of the old one is kept, so read it first with settings_send_as_get. An empty signature clears it. Gmail mailboxes only: an Outlook mailbox exposes no signature to write.

tools.name: settings_send_as_get
tools.description: Read the signature on the mailbox's own send-as identity, as HTML. A mailbox with no signature answers without one. Gmail mailboxes only: an Outlook mailbox exposes no signature to read.

tools.name: settings_get_vacation
tools.description: Read whether a connected mailbox answers mail automatically, what it says, and any schedule or restriction it carries.

tools.name: settings_update_vacation
tools.description: Turn the vacation responder on or off. A Gmail mailbox replaces the whole responder, so a schedule or a restriction it already held is not kept; an Outlook mailbox keeps what this call does not name, and holds no subject.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mail" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: messages_list, messages_list_all_mailboxes, threads_get, messages_get, labels_delete, threads_archive, messages_attachments_get, settings_send_as_get · Private data: drafts_forward, messages_forward, messages_attachments_get, settings_filters_list, settings_filters_create · Public sink: drafts_forward, messages_send, drafts_send, messages_reply, messages_forward, settings_send_as_patch, settings_send_as_get · Destructive: drafts_update, drafts_delete, labels_delete, threads_modify, settings_filters_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: messages_list, messages_list_all_mailboxes, threads_get, messages_get, labels_delete, threads_archive, messages_attachments_get, settings_send_as_get · Private data: drafts_forward, messages_forward, messages_attachments_get, settings_filters_list, settings_filters_create · Public sink: drafts_forward, messages_send, drafts_send, messages_reply, messages_forward, settings_send_as_patch, settings_send_as_get · Destructive: drafts_update, drafts_delete, labels_delete, threads_modify, settings_filters_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "drafts_update" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

A field the call leaves out stays as the draft has it. A mailbox whose provider is imap keeps the edited draft under a new id the answer names, and the old id then reads nothing; an old version its server did not remove stays in Drafts, named as previousVersion"
